claims.claim: The BTB is not functional in P180 (120 datx) Sox9/8 mutant testes.
claims.source: Cldn11 (the claudin11 gene) expression was similar between controls and double mutants before P150 (90 datx) (not shown), but it was severely reduced by P150 (90 datx) and completely absent in P180 (120 datx) Sox9/8 mutant testes (Figure 1Dg–i), indicating that the BTB is not functional in these testes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the loss of Claudin11 expression and confirmed by biotin tracer experiments.

claims.claim: Control testes had a functional BTB, whereas that of the mutant testes had become permeable.
claims.source: To proof this assumption, we tested the permeability of the BTB of P120 (60 datx) mice with a biotin tracer experiment revealing that control testes had a functional BTB, whereas that of the mutant testes had become permeable (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by biotin tracer experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claims.claim: Spermatogenesis becomes disrupted in testes with Sertoli cells deficient for both Sox9 and Sox8.
claims.source: These results indicate that spermatogenesis becomes disrupted in testes with Sertoli cells deficient for both Sox9 and Sox8.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from immunofluorescence data showing loss of spermatocytes and spermatogonia in mutant testes.

claims.claim: Leydig cells do not transdifferentiate into theca cells in Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice.
claims.source: Unlike other somatic cells, Leydig cells appear not to be seriously affected in testes from Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice. These cells do not transdifferentiate into theca cells, as they never express Foxl2 (as theca cells do; not shown), and maintain the steroidogenic function for a long time after Sox9 ablation, as deduced from the expression of P450scc, a cytochrome involved in the synthesis of testosterone (Figure 1Dm,n).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the absence of Foxl2 expression in Leydig cells.

claims.claim: Leydig cells maintain the steroidogenic function for a long time after Sox9 ablation in Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice.
claims.source: Unlike other somatic cells, Leydig cells appear not to be seriously affected in testes from Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice. These cells do not transdifferentiate into theca cells, as they never express Foxl2 (as theca cells do; not shown), and maintain the steroidogenic function for a long time after Sox9 ablation, as deduced from the expression of P450scc, a cytochrome involved in the synthesis of testosterone (Figure 1Dm,n).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by P450scc expression shown in Figure 1Dm,n.

claims.claim: At P90 (30 datx), FOXL2 protein was almost completely absent from mutant testes.
claims.source: At P90 (30 datx), FOXL2 protein was almost completely absent from mutant testes.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: By P105 (45 datx), FOXL2-positive cells were present in almost all testis cords of Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice.
claims.source: However, by P105 (45 datx), positive cells were present in almost all testis cords, and by P150 (90 datx), the most severely affected mice showed many FOXL2-positive cells within almost all testis cords (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: SC-DKO testes exhibit a striking feminization of the testicular transcriptome.
claims.source: Our results show that SC-DKO testes exhibit a striking feminization of the testicular transcriptome.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by genome-wide transcriptome analysis showing upregulation of ovarian genes.

claims.claim: Most genes in mutant testes adopted an ovary-like expression pattern.
claims.source: With the exception of a few gene clusters, most genes in mutant testes adopted an ovary-like expression pattern (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the heat map in Figure 2B showing gene expression patterns.

claims.claim: The cell reprogramming observed in the SC-DKO testes only affects somatic cells.
claims.source: Expression heat maps for selected 39 ovarian somatic cell-specific genes and 33 oocyte-specific genes selected using bioGPS (biogps.gnf.org) revealed that the cell reprogramming observed in the SC-DKO testes only affects somatic cells (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by expression heat maps in Figure 2C showing upregulation of somatic but not oocyte genes.

claims.claim: Six genes known to be adult granulosa cell markers were upregulated in the mutant Sertoli cells.
claims.source: Notably, bar plots for six genes known to be adult granulosa cell markers showed that these genes were upregulated in the mutant Sertoli cells, revealing an ovary-like expression pattern (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by bar plots in Figure 2D showing upregulation of granulosa cell markers.

claims.claim: Within the seminiferous cords of SC-DKO testes, a few FOXL2+ cells expressing the enzyme aromatase were found.
claims.source: In addition, within the seminiferous cords of SC-DKO testes we found a few FOXL2+ cells expressing the enzyme aromatase (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: FOXL2+ cells in Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes originate from Sox9/8 null Sertoli cells.
claims.source: We next investigated the origin of the granulosa-like, FOXL2+ cells present in the Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes. Several pieces of evidence show that FOXL2+ cells in our mutant testes originate from Sox9/8 null Sertoli cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including Cre-reporter expression and WT1 expression patterns.

claims.claim: FOXL2+ cells always located inside testis cords with strong expression of the Cre-recombination reporter EYFP.
claims.source: Importantly, we found that FOXL2+ cells always located inside testis cords with strong expression of the Cre-recombination reporter EYFP (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes experience a cell-autonomous Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation.
claims.source: Altogether, these results indicate that Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes experience a cell-autonomous Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation which triggers the observed testis-to-ovary genetic reprogramming in these gonads.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that FOXL2+ cells originate from Sertoli cells expressing Cre.

claims.claim: Cells coexpressing SOX9 and FOXL2 were rare at any stage analyzed in Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes.
claims.source: We found that cells coexpressing SOX9 and FOXL2 were rare at any stage analyzed [12 out of 203 FOXL2+ cells co-expressed SOX9 at P120 (60 datx)] (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating that Foxl2 upregulation requires previous elimination of both SOXE proteins.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Foxl2 upregulation requires previous elimination of both SOXE proteins.
claims.source: We found that cells coexpressing SOX9 and FOXL2 were rare at any stage analyzed [12 out of 203 FOXL2+ cells co-expressed SOX9 at P120 (60 datx)] (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating that Foxl2 upregulation requires previous elimination of both SOXE proteins.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the rarity of cells coexpressing SOX9 and FOXL2.

claims.claim: Mutant Sertoli cells showed varying degrees of both SOX9 and DMRT1 staining intensity, although they normally paralleled each other in intensity.
claims.source: Whereas all Sertoli cells in control testes showed strong staining for both DMRT1 and SOX9 (SS, Figure 4Ba), mutant Sertoli cells showed varying degrees of both SOX9 and DMRT1 staining intensity, although they normally paralleled each other in intensity.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by triple immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Dmrt1 is downregulated after Sox9 ablation in SC-DKO testes.
claims.source: Double WT1-DMRT1 staining confirmed that as early as at P90 (30 datx) many WT1+ cells (Sertoli cells) have already lost DMRT1 expression (green cells in Figure 4Cb), showing that Dmrt1 is downregulated after Sox9 ablation and before Wt1 downregulation occurs in SC-DKO testes.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4Cb.

claims.claim: DMRT1 and FOXL2 only colocalize in a reduced number of cells in the testes of Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice.
claims.source: In addition, as observed for SOX9 and FOXL2 (see above), DMRT1 and FOXL2 only colocalize in a reduced number of cells in the testes of our Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice [16 out of 127 FOXL2+ cells co-expressed DMRT1 at P120 (60 datx)] (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: SOX9 and SOX8 are necessary for the maintenance of Dmrt1 expression in adult Sertoli cells.
claims.source: Overall, these findings support the notion that SOX9 and SOX8 are necessary for the maintenance of Dmrt1 expression in adult Sertoli cells and that these testis-promoting factors negatively regulate Foxl2.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that DMRT1 is lost in Sox9/8 mutant cells.

claims.claim: SOX9 and SOX8 negatively regulate Foxl2 in adult Sertoli cells.
claims.source: Overall, these findings support the notion that SOX9 and SOX8 are necessary for the maintenance of Dmrt1 expression in adult Sertoli cells and that these testis-promoting factors negatively regulate Foxl2.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that FOXL2 is upregulated after Sox9/8 ablation.

claims.claim: Nearly all genes strongly affected by the loss of DMRT1 were also affected by the loss of SOX9/8.
claims.source: Nearly all genes strongly affected by the loss of Dmrt1 were also affected by the loss of Sox9/8 (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison of transcriptome data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Both Dmrt1 and Sox9/8 act in the same pathway.
claims.source: This finding suggests that both Dmrt1 and Sox9/8 act in the same pathway, although the possibility also exists that this coincidence between both gene expression patterns could be a secondary effect of the change in relative numbers of cell types in the SC-Sox9/8 DKO testes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the similarity in gene expression changes between Dmrt1 and Sox9/8 mutants.

claims.claim: A set of genes belonging to the RA-signaling pathway showed similar misexpression in both SC-Dmrt1 KO and SC-Sox9/8 DKO testes.
claims.source: By comparing the mRNA profiling of SC-Dmrt1 KO and SC-Sox9/8 DKO testes, we found a set of genes belonging to the RA-signaling pathway showing similar misexpression in both mutants (Figure 5A, green dots, Figure 5—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison of transcriptome data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Treatment with WIN 18,446 resulted in a 3.5-fold reduction in the number of FOXL2-positive cells per testis cord section in Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice.
claims.source: We found a 3.5-fold reduction in the number of FOXL2-positive cells per testis cord section in the WIN 18,446-treated mice (1.80 ± 2.03), compared to the vehicle (DMSO)-injected controls (6.57 ± 3.52; p<0.001; Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 3).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative data from WIN 18,446 treatment experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The process of Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation is inhibited when RA levels were reduced in Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice.
claims.source: Hence, as reported for Dmrt1 SC-KO mice (Minkina et al., 2014), the process of Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation seems to be also inhibited when RA levels were reduced in our study model.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the reduction in FOXL2+ cells after WIN 18,446 treatment.

claims.claim: The numbers of TUNEL-positive cells in Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes were significantly higher than those found in TX-treated control testes.
claims.source: The numbers of TUNEL-positive cells counted in a total area of 11.55 mm2 between P90 (30 datx) and P120 (60 datx) in both SC-DKO mutants (370 cells for the Wt1-CreERT2 line and 488 cells for the Sox9-CreERT2 line) were significantly higher than those found in TX-treated control testes (120 cells; goodness of fit test p<2.2e-16 in both cases; Figure 6Aa–c, Figure 6—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Neither SOX9- nor FOXL2-expressing cells were observed to be apoptotic in mutant testes before P120 (60 datx).
claims.source: Neither SOX9- nor FOXL2-expressing cells were observed to be apoptotic in mutant testes before P120 (60 datx) (Figure 6Ba,c), but SOX9+ cells were found to be apoptotic in the P150 (90 datx) testes (Figure 6Bb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence with TUNEL shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Apoptotic cells expressing WT1 were observed as early as P90 (30 datx) in Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes.
claims.source: In contrast, we observed apoptotic cells expressing WT1 as early as P90 (30 datx) (Figure 6Bd), indicating that apoptosis mainly affects recombined Sertoli cells in which Sox9 had been ablated but Foxl2 had not yet been upregulated.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by double immunofluorescence with TUNEL shown in Figure 6Bd.

claims.claim: Apoptosis mainly affects recombined Sertoli cells in which Sox9 had been ablated but Foxl2 had not yet been upregulated.
claims.source: In contrast, we observed apoptotic cells expressing WT1 as early as P90 (30 datx) (Figure 6Bd), indicating that apoptosis mainly affects recombined Sertoli cells in which Sox9 had been ablated but Foxl2 had not yet been upregulated.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that WT1+ cells undergo apoptosis early, while SOX9+ and FOXL2+ cells do not.

claims.claim: Testis regression in Sox9/8 mutants occurs in two different stages.
claims.source: Altogether, these findings suggest that testis regression in Sox9/8 mutants occurs in two different stages.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the temporal pattern of apoptosis affecting different cell types at different times.

claims.claim: During the first two months after the initiation of TX administration, both non-recombined Sertoli cells (SOX9+) and transdifferentiated cells (FOXL2+) remain alive, whereas recombined but not yet transdifferentiated cells (SOX9−, WT1+) do undergo apoptosis.
claims.source: During the first two months after the initiation of TX administration, both non-recombined Sertoli cells (SOX9+) and transdifferentiated cells (FOXL2+) remain alive, whereas recombined but not yet transdifferentiated cells (SOX9− , WT1+) do undergo apoptosis.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the temporal pattern of apoptosis shown by TUNEL assays combined with marker expression.

claims.claim: In the second stage (P180 and older mice), massive apoptosis affects all cell types, including the remaining Sertoli cells and granulosa-like cells.
claims.source: In the second stage (P180 and older mice), massive apoptosis affects all cell types, including the remaining Sertoli cells and granulosa-like cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of SOX9+ apoptotic cells at P150 and the presence of apoptotic bodies.

claims.claim: The bipotential nature of the genital ridge at the beginning of gonad development is not completely lost once either testes or ovaries acquire their final adult morphology and functionality.
claims.source: There is now compelling evidence that the bipotential nature of the genital ridge at the beginning of gonad development is not completely lost once either testes or ovaries acquire their final adult morphology and functionality.
claims.evidence: This is a general statement supported by the findings of the study and previous literature.

claims.claim: Sox9 has a crucial role in adult testis maintenance.
claims.source: These results evidence that Sox9 has a crucial role, not only during sex determination and testis differentiation, but also in adult testis maintenance, where, together with Sox8 and coordinately with Dmrt1, it prevents male-to-female genetic reprogramming.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the combined data.

claims.claim: Sox9 expression is independent of DMRT1 during sex determination and some time thereafter.
claims.source: Thus, Sox9 expression is independent of DMRT1 during sex determination and some time thereafter.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that early embryonic Dmrt1 KO mice have normal Sox9 expression.

claims.claim: Sox9 expression is independent of Dmrt1 in newly differentiated Sertoli cells.
claims.source: This suggests again that Sox9 expression is independent of Dmrt1 in newly differentiated Sertoli cells and that the loss of Sox9 after Dmrt1 ablation is a secondary consequence of the upregulation of ovarian genes(s), such as Foxl2, in the same cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the delayed Sox9 downregulation after Dmrt1 ablation.

claims.claim: In the adult gonad, mutant Sox9/8 Sertoli cells lose DMRT1, and FOXL2 protein appears concomitant with the loss of DMRT1.
claims.source: Here we provide evidence that in the adult gonad, mutant Sox9/8 Sertoli cells lose DMRT1, and that FOXL2 protein appears concomitant with the loss of DMRT1, consistent with the notion that Dmrt1 expression is SOX9/8-dependent and that DMTR1 represses Foxl2.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data showing temporal patterns of DMRT1 and FOXL2 expression.

claims.claim: Dmrt1 expression is SOX9/8-dependent in the adult testis.
claims.source: Here we provide evidence that in the adult gonad, mutant Sox9/8 Sertoli cells lose DMRT1, and that FOXL2 protein appears concomitant with the loss of DMRT1, consistent with the notion that Dmrt1 expression is SOX9/8-dependent and that DMTR1 represses Foxl2.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that DMRT1 is lost in Sox9/8 mutant cells.

claims.claim: DMRT1 represses Foxl2 in the adult testis.
claims.source: Here we provide evidence that in the adult gonad, mutant Sox9/8 Sertoli cells lose DMRT1, and that FOXL2 protein appears concomitant with the loss of DMRT1, consistent with the notion that Dmrt1 expression is SOX9/8-dependent and that DMTR1 represses Foxl2.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that FOXL2 appears after DMRT1 is lost.

claims.claim: A main role for SOX9/8 in adult male sex maintenance is to keep Dmrt1 actively expressed.
claims.source: Altogether, available data suggest that, like at earlier stages, a main role for SOX9/8 in adult male sex maintenance is to keep Dmrt1 actively expressed, this latter gene having a fundamental role in repressing female-specific genes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing that DMRT1 is lost in Sox9/8 mutants and that this leads to upregulation of female genes.

claims.claim: Dmrt1 has a fundamental role in repressing female-specific genes in the adult testis.
claims.source: Altogether, available data suggest that, like at earlier stages, a main role for SOX9/8 in adult male sex maintenance is to keep Dmrt1 actively expressed, this latter gene having a fundamental role in repressing female-specific genes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that female genes are upregulated when DMRT1 is lost.

claims.claim: Wt1 acts upstream of both Sox9 and Sox8 during the early stages of embryonic testis development.
claims.source: There is evidence that Wt1 acts upstream of both Sox9 and Sox8 during the early stages of embryonic testis development (Gao et al., 2006; Barrionuevo et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Sox9/8-depleted Sertoli cells initially maintain WT1 expression, but this expression becomes progressively downregulated coinciding with the time-point at which Foxl2 is upregulated.
claims.source: In the adult testis, we have seen that Sox9/8-depleted Sertoli cells initially maintain WT1 expression, but this expression becomes progressively downregulated coinciding with the time-point at which Foxl2 is upregulated.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence data showing temporal patterns of WT1 and FOXL2 expression.

claims.claim: Wt1 retains its hierarchical position in the adult testis.
claims.source: This suggests that Wt1 retains its hierarchical position also in the adult testis, and that female-specific factors, including Foxl2, may be involved in its silencing.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that WT1 is downregulated after Foxl2 upregulation.

claims.claim: Female-specific factors, including Foxl2, may be involved in silencing Wt1 in the adult testis.
claims.source: This suggests that Wt1 retains its hierarchical position also in the adult testis, and that female-specific factors, including Foxl2, may be involved in its silencing.
claims.evidence: This is speculative, inferred from the temporal correlation between Foxl2 upregulation and Wt1 downregulation.

claims.claim: Transdifferentiation of Sox9/8 SC-DKO Sertoli cells seems to give rise to mature follicle-type granulosa cells.
claims.source: Thus, considering these two molecular markers, transdifferentiation of Sox9/8 SC-DKO Sertoli cells seems to give rise to mature follicle-type granulosa cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that transdifferentiated cells express FOXL2 but not WT1, similar to mature follicle granulosa cells.

claims.claim: WT1 may play an anti-feminizing role in adult Sertoli cells.
claims.source: This expression pattern also suggests that WT1 may play an anti-feminizing role in adult Sertoli cells.
claims.evidence: This is speculative, inferred from the observation that WT1 is lost during transdifferentiation.

claims.claim: The functional redundancy between the Sox9 and Sox8 alleles observed in embryonic Sertoli cells is also maintained in adult Sertoli cells.
claims.source: We have reported here that the functional redundancy between the Sox9 and Sox8 alleles observed in embryonic Sertoli cells (Barrionuevo et al., 2009) and other embryonic cell types (Chaboisier et al., 2004; Stolt et al., 2004; Reginensi et al., 2011) is also maintained in adult Sertoli cells.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the observation that the phenotype severity increases with the number of mutant alleles.

claims.claim: Sox9/8 initially protects Sertoli cells from apoptosis.
claims.source: Consistently, we found no SOX9+ apoptotic cell by P90 (30 datx), indicating that Sox9/8 initially protects Sertoli cells from apoptosis, a role previously shown for this gene in other developing organs (Akiyama et al., 2002; Cheung et al., 2005; Seymour et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the absence of SOX9+ apoptotic cells early in the time course.

claims.claim: Adult testis tubules require the presence of a minimum number of Sertoli cells to be maintained.
claims.source: It is well known that the number of Sertoli cells must reach a critical threshold to organize embryonic testicular cords (Palmer and Burgoyne, 1991; Schmahl and Capel, 2003). Accordingly, our results suggest that adult testis tubules also require the presence of a minimum number of Sertoli cells to be maintained.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that testis tubules degenerate when Sertoli cell numbers fall below a threshold.

claims.claim: SOXE factors are necessary to maintain Sertoli cell identity and seminiferous tubule integrity.
claims.source: Hence, our results show that SOXE factors are necessary to maintain Sertoli cell identity and seminiferous tubule integrity, as these cells maintain all the other cell types forming the tubules, which become completely disorganized in their absence.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that seminiferous tubules degenerate after Sox9/8 ablation.

claims.claim: Deregulation of important structural proteins controlled by SoxE genes could be involved in the process of testis degeneration.
claims.source: Several findings suggest that deregulation of important structural proteins controlled by SoxE genes could be involved in the process.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of altered expression of structural proteins in mutant testes.

claims.claim: After Sox9 ablation in Sox8 mutants, both developing and adult testes experience downregulation and/or abnormal distribution of several important proteins required for the formation of Sertoli–Sertoli and/or Sertoli–germ cell adhesion complexes.
claims.source: Also, after Sox9 ablation in Sox8 mutants, both developing (Barrionuevo et al., 2009; Georg et al., 2012) and adult testes (present paper) experience downregulation and/or abnormal distribution of several important proteins required for the formation of Sertoli–Sertoli and/or Sertoli–germ cell adhesion complexes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and supported by citations.

claims.claim: Spermatogenesis is halted when the functionality of the BTB is impaired.
claims.source: In this context, it is noteworthy that spermatogenesis is halted when the functionality of the BTB is impaired (Meng et al., 2005; Dadhich et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: In Sox9/8 SC-DKO mouse testes, BTB permeation and cytoskeleton impairment may give rise to a damaged intra-tubular microenvironment in which spermatogenesis is not supported anymore.
claims.source: Thus, in our Sox9/8 SC-DKO mouse testes, BTB permeation and cytoskeleton impairment may give rise to a damaged intra-tubular microenvironment in which spermatogenesis is not supported anymore, germ cells undergoing both apoptosis and desquamation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of BTB permeability and loss of spermatogenesis.

claims.claim: Failure of Sox9/8 double mutant Sertoli cells to sustain testis tubule architecture is a direct consequence of altered expression of cell adhesion molecules and probably of other structural elements such as components of the cytoskeleton or the extracellular matrix.
claims.source: Altogether, available data strongly suggest that failure of Sox9/8 double mutant Sertoli cells to sustain testis tubule architecture is a direct consequence of altered expression of cell adhesion molecules and probably of other structural elements such as components of the cytoskeleton or the extracellular matrix.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on structural protein expression and testis degeneration.

claims.claim: Adult PM cells retain their original dependence from Sertoli cells.
claims.source: Our results in the adult testis show that adult PM cells retain their original dependence from Sertoli cells, whereas maintenance of adult Leydig cells is again Sertoli cell-independent.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that PM cells are lost while Leydig cells persist in mutant testes.

claims.claim: Maintenance of adult Leydig cells is Sertoli cell-independent.
claims.source: Our results in the adult testis show that adult PM cells retain their original dependence from Sertoli cells, whereas maintenance of adult Leydig cells is again Sertoli cell-independent.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Leydig cells persist and maintain function in mutant testes.

claims.claim: Sox9/8 play a central role in maintaining active Dmrt1 in the adult testis.
claims.source: According to the above considerations, we propose a model for the maintenance of Sertoli cell fate in the adult testis. In this model, Sox9/8 play a central role in maintaining active Dmrt1, which prevents expression of ovary promoting genes, including Foxl2, which in turn negatively regulates Sox9/8 and/or Dmrt1.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the combined data from the study.

claims.claim: Dmrt1 prevents expression of ovary promoting genes, including Foxl2.
claims.source: In this model, Sox9/8 play a central role in maintaining active Dmrt1, which prevents expression of ovary promoting genes, including Foxl2, which in turn negatively regulates Sox9/8 and/or Dmrt1.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the combined data from the study.

claims.claim: Foxl2 negatively regulates Sox9/8 and/or Dmrt1 in the adult testis.
claims.source: In this model, Sox9/8 play a central role in maintaining active Dmrt1, which prevents expression of ovary promoting genes, including Foxl2, which in turn negatively regulates Sox9/8 and/or Dmrt1.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the combined data from the study and previous literature.

claims.claim: Dmrt1 inhibits RA signaling which promotes the expression of Foxl2.
claims.source: Dmrt1 inhibits RA signaling which promotes the expression of Foxl2, although an interference of Sox9 on this signaling pathway, through a Dmrt1-independent mechanism, cannot be ruled out.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the WIN 18,446 treatment data and previous literature.

claims.claim: Wt1 positively regulates Sox8/9 in the adult testis.
claims.source: Wt1 positively regulates Sox8/9 and is negatively regulated by Foxl2 and/or other ovarian-specific genes.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the temporal patterns of gene expression observed in the study.

claims.claim: Wt1 is negatively regulated by Foxl2 and/or other ovarian-specific genes in the adult testis.
claims.source: Wt1 positively regulates Sox8/9 and is negatively regulated by Foxl2 and/or other ovarian-specific genes.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the temporal patterns of gene expression observed in the study.

claims.claim: Sox9/8 are needed for maintaining the expression of important testis structural genes.
claims.source: Sox9/8 are also needed for maintaining the expression of important testis structural genes and for protecting Sertoli cells from apoptosis (Figure 7, solid lines).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by data showing altered expression of structural proteins and increased apoptosis in mutant testes.

claims.claim: Sox9/8 have important DMRT1-dependent and independent functions in the maintenance of the adult testis.
claims.source: In conclusion, we have shown Sox9/8 have important DMRT1-dependent and independent functions in the maintenance of the adult testis.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the combined data.

claims.claim: In the absence of Sox9 and Sox8, phenotypically normal, fertile testes are genetically reprogrammed and Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation occurs.
claims.source: In their absence, phenotypically normal, fertile testes are genetically reprogrammed and Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation occurs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claims.claim: Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation is a transient stage of mutant adult Sertoli cells in the irreversible degenerative process the seminiferous tubules face in the absence of Sox9 and Sox8.
claims.source: Nevertheless, this is a mere transient stage of mutant adult Sertoli cells in the irreversible degenerative process the seminiferous tubules face in the absence of Sox9 and Sox8.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that transdifferentiated cells eventually undergo apoptosis and tubules degenerate completely.

results.result: Ablation of Sox9 in adult Sox8-/- mice leads to testis-to-ovary genetic reprogramming and Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation. FOXL2+ cells appear by P105 (45 datx) and increase by P150 (90 datx). Transcriptome analysis shows feminization with upregulation of ovarian somatic genes but not oocyte genes. FOXL2+ cells originate from Sox9/8-null Sertoli cells as demonstrated by Cre-reporter colocalization.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C3, C28, C48-57, and C111 collectively demonstrate testis-to-ovary reprogramming and Sertoli-to-granulosa transdifferentiation through multiple converging lines of evidence: temporal appearance of FOXL2+ cells (immunofluorescence), genome-wide transcriptome feminization showing upregulation of granulosa markers, and lineage tracing showing FOXL2+ cells originate from Cre+ Sertoli cells. The data are internally consistent and well-supported by figures.

results.result: Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes undergo progressive degeneration culminating in acellular seminiferous tubules. SOX9+ cell numbers decrease significantly (37-69% reduction at P150), structural proteins (CLAUDIN11, ACTA2) are lost, the blood-testis barrier becomes permeable, and spermatogenesis is disrupted. Phenotype severity correlates with the number of mutant alleles.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C33-45 are well-supported by quantitative cell counts (C36-37), immunofluorescence for structural markers (C39-42), biotin tracer experiments demonstrating BTB permeability (C43-44), and histological analysis showing progressive tubule degeneration. The dose-dependent effect (C38) strengthens the causal relationship. Multiple independent measures converge on the conclusion of testis degeneration.

results.result: SOX9/8 maintain Dmrt1 expression in adult Sertoli cells, and DMRT1 loss precedes FOXL2 upregulation. DMRT1 is lost in Sox9/8 mutant cells by P90 (30 datx), and cells coexpressing SOX9/DMRT1 with FOXL2 are rare (12/203 for SOX9+FOXL2+; 16/127 for DMRT1+FOXL2+), indicating that FOXL2 upregulation requires elimination of both SOX9/8 and DMRT1.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-6, C31, C58-64, C81-83 are supported by immunofluorescence showing temporal patterns: DMRT1 is lost in Sox9/8 mutant cells early (P90), and FOXL2 appears later with minimal colocalization. The quantitative data on rare coexpression (C58, C62) strengthens the conclusion that FOXL2 upregulation requires prior loss of testis-promoting factors. The temporal sequence is clearly demonstrated.

results.result: Testis-to-ovary reprogramming in Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes is retinoic acid (RA)-mediated and occurs as a consequence of Dmrt1 downregulation. Nearly all genes affected by Dmrt1 loss are also affected by Sox9/8 loss, including RA-signaling pathway genes. WIN 18,446 treatment (RA synthesis inhibitor) resulted in 3.5-fold reduction in FOXL2+ cells (p<0.001).
results.evaluation: Claims C29-30, C65-69, C106 are supported by transcriptome comparison showing overlap between Dmrt1 and Sox9/8 mutant gene expression patterns (C65), identification of RA pathway genes (C67), and pharmacological inhibition experiments with WIN 18,446 showing significant reduction in FOXL2+ cells (C68-69). The WIN 18,446 experiment provides functional validation of the RA-mediated mechanism, though the authors acknowledge Sox9 may also act through Dmrt1-independent mechanisms.

results.result: Sox9/8 protect Sertoli cells from apoptosis and control expression of structural proteins. TUNEL+ cells are significantly higher in mutants (370-488 cells) versus controls (120 cells, p<2.2e-16). Apoptosis occurs in two stages: early apoptosis affects recombined Sox9/8-deficient, WT1+ cells (P90), while SOX9+ and FOXL2+ cells remain viable until later stages (P150+).
results.evaluation: Claims C7-8, C70-76, C93, C109 are supported by quantitative TUNEL assays showing significantly increased apoptosis in mutants (C70) and double immunofluorescence identifying which cell types undergo apoptosis at different timepoints (C71-73). The two-stage model (C74-76) is well-supported by temporal analysis. The anti-apoptotic role is consistent with prior literature (C93). The data on structural protein expression (C7) is supported by immunofluorescence results.

results.result: Sox9, together with Sox8 and coordinately with Dmrt1, controls adult testis maintenance. The authors propose a regulatory model where Sox9/8 maintain Dmrt1 expression, which prevents expression of ovary-promoting genes including Foxl2. Wt1 positively regulates Sox9/8 and is negatively regulated by Foxl2. Sox9/8 have both DMRT1-dependent and independent functions.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C78, C84-85, C103-105, C107-108, C110 represent the main conclusions and proposed regulatory model. These are well-supported by the combined data showing: (1) DMRT1 loss in Sox9/8 mutants, (2) FOXL2 upregulation after DMRT1 loss, (3) RA-mediated mechanism, (4) temporal patterns of WT1 expression, and (5) structural and apoptotic phenotypes. The model integrates multiple lines of evidence, though some regulatory relationships (dashed lines in Figure 7) are acknowledged as less certain.

results.result: Leydig cells do not transdifferentiate and maintain steroidogenic function in Sox9/8 SC-DKO mice, while peritubular myoid (PM) cells are lost. Leydig cells never express Foxl2 and continue expressing P450scc, HSD17b3, and Insl3, indicating maintenance of adult Leydig cells is Sertoli cell-independent.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-47, C101-102 are supported by immunofluorescence showing absence of Foxl2 in Leydig cells (C46), persistent P450scc expression (C47), and transcriptome data showing maintained expression of Leydig markers (HSD17b3, Insl3). The differential behavior of PM cells (lost) versus Leydig cells (maintained) is demonstrated by ACTA2 staining patterns (C40-41). The conclusion about Sertoli cell-independence is a reasonable inference.

results.result: Sox9 expression is independent of Dmrt1 during sex determination and in newly differentiated Sertoli cells. In adult Sox9/8 SC-DKO testes, WT1 is initially maintained but progressively downregulated coinciding with Foxl2 upregulation. Transdifferentiated cells resemble mature follicle-type granulosa cells (FOXL2+, WT1-), suggesting WT1 may play an anti-feminizing role.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-80, C86-91 are supported by citations to prior work showing Sox9 independence from Dmrt1 during development (C79-80, C86) and by immunofluorescence data showing temporal patterns of WT1 and FOXL2 expression in the current study (C87). The characterization of transdifferentiated cells as mature follicle-type (C90) is based on marker expression patterns compared to control ovary. The speculation about WT1's anti-feminizing role (C91) is appropriately qualified as a suggestion.

results.result: Functional redundancy between Sox9 and Sox8 alleles is maintained in adult Sertoli cells. Failure of Sox9/8 mutant Sertoli cells to sustain testis tubule architecture is attributed to altered expression of cell adhesion molecules, structural proteins, and BTB components. Adult testis tubules require a minimum number of Sertoli cells to be maintained.
results.evaluation: Claims C92, C94-100 are supported by dose-dependent phenotype severity correlating with mutant allele number (C92, C38), immunofluorescence showing altered expression of adhesion and structural proteins (C97), BTB permeability data (C98-99), and progressive loss of Sertoli cells leading to complete tubule collapse (C94). The mechanistic interpretation linking structural protein deregulation to tubule degeneration (C96, C100) is well-supported by the data, though some aspects remain inferential.

results.result: Background claims establishing prior knowledge about SoxE genes, sex determination pathways, sexual antagonism during development, and adult gonad plasticity. These include the roles of Sox9/Sox8 in testis development, the antagonism between male (SRY/SOX9/DMRT1) and female (WNT/β-catenin/FOXL2) pathways, and previous observations of transdifferentiation in adult gonads.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C10-27, C77 are background statements supported by citations to prior literature. These establish the context for the current study and are appropriately referenced. C1 specifically notes that while Sox9/Sox8 are required for postnatal fertility, their role in the adult testis had not been investigated, justifying the current work.

results.result: Sertoli-to-granulosa cell transdifferentiation is a transient stage in the irreversible degenerative process that seminiferous tubules undergo in the absence of Sox9 and Sox8, as transdifferentiated cells eventually undergo apoptosis and tubules degenerate completely.
results.evaluation: Claim C112 is supported by the temporal data showing that while FOXL2+ cells appear and increase initially (P105-P150), they do not prevent continued degeneration, and by P180+ massive apoptosis affects all cell types including transdifferentiated cells (C76), ultimately resulting in acellular tubules (C4). This interpretation is consistent with the two-stage apoptosis model (C74-76).
